significance: A remote Nyingma monastery at about 8,000 feet in Upper Dzongu, inside the buffer zone of Khangchendzonga National Park, first raised under Chogyal Phuntsog Namgyal II and built in its present form in 1789 by Pema Dechhen Gyatso, with the standing structure reconstructed in 1980. It safeguards manuscripts and relics carried here during the Gorkha invasions, shown to the public only once every three years at the Kamsil ceremony in April.
story: The site is held to have been revealed as sacred ground in 1760 by the fourth Lhatsun, Kunzang Jigmed Gyatso.
